name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  create-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Extract version from tag
        id: version
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Verify tag matches Cargo.toml version
        run: |
          CARGO_VERSION=$(grep '^version' Cargo.toml | head -1 | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
          if [ "${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}" != "$CARGO_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "::error::Tag version (${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}) does not match Cargo.toml version ($CARGO_VERSION)"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Create release in replay-releases
        run: |
          gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" \
            --repo skillsynchq/replay-releases \
            --draft \
            --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" \
            --notes "Release $GITHUB_REF_NAME"
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASES_PAT }}

  build-release:
    needs: create-release
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            os: ubuntu-latest
            use_cross: true
          - target: aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
            os: ubuntu-latest
            use_cross: true
          - target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-latest
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-latest
          - target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            os: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Install cross
        if: matrix.use_cross
        run: |
          curl -sSfL "https://github.com/cross-rs/cross/releases/download/v0.2.5/cross-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz" \
            | tar xz -C /usr/local/bin

      - name: Build
        env:
          REPLAY_SERVER_URL: https://replay.md
        run: ${{ matrix.use_cross && 'cross' || 'cargo' }} build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Package (unix)
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          ARCHIVE="replay-cli-v${{ needs.create-release.outputs.version }}-${{ matrix.target }}"
          mkdir "$ARCHIVE"
          cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/replay" "$ARCHIVE/"
          tar czf "$ARCHIVE.tar.gz" "$ARCHIVE"
          shasum -a 256 "$ARCHIVE.tar.gz" > "$ARCHIVE.tar.gz.sha256"
          echo "ASSET=$ARCHIVE.tar.gz" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "CHECKSUM=$ARCHIVE.tar.gz.sha256" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Package (windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          ARCHIVE="replay-cli-v${{ needs.create-release.outputs.version }}-${{ matrix.target }}"
          mkdir "$ARCHIVE"
          cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/replay.exe" "$ARCHIVE/"
          7z a "$ARCHIVE.zip" "$ARCHIVE"
          certutil -hashfile "$ARCHIVE.zip" SHA256 | head -2 | tail -1 > "$ARCHIVE.zip.sha256"
          echo "ASSET=$ARCHIVE.zip" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "CHECKSUM=$ARCHIVE.zip.sha256" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Upload to replay-releases
        shell: bash
        run: |
          gh release upload "v${{ needs.create-release.outputs.version }}" \
            "$ASSET" "$CHECKSUM" \
            --repo skillsynchq/replay-releases
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASES_PAT }}

  publish-release:
    needs: [create-release, build-release]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Mark release as published
        run: |
          gh release edit "v${{ needs.create-release.outputs.version }}" \
            --repo skillsynchq/replay-releases \
            --draft=false
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RELEASES_PAT }}

[package]
name = "replay-cli"
version = "0.3.2"
edition = "2021"
description = "Share AI coding conversations as reviewable threads."
authors = ["SkillSync"]
license = "Apache-2.0"
homepage = "https://replay.md"
repository = "https://github.com/skillsynchq/replay-cli"
readme = "README.md"
keywords = ["cli", "tui", "claude-code", "codex", "ai"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "development-tools"]

[package.metadata.binstall]
pkg-url = "https://github.com/skillsynchq/replay-releases/releases/download/v{ version }/{ name }-v{ version }-{ target }{ archive-suffix }"
bin-dir = "{ bin }{ binary-ext }"
pkg-fmt = "tgz"

[package.metadata.binstall.overrides.'cfg(target_os = "windows")']
pkg-fmt = "zip"

[profile.release]
strip = true
lto = true

[[bin]]
name = "replay"
path = "src/main.rs"

[features]
default = ["auth"]
auth = ["dep:tiny_http", "dep:reqwest", "dep:open", "dep:rand"]

[dependencies]
anyhow = "1"
chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }
clap_complete = "4"
console = "0.16.3"
ctrlc = "3.5.2"
dialoguer = "0.12.0"
dirs = "6"
open = { version = "5", optional = true }
rand = { version = "0.9", optional = true }
base64 = "0.22"
flate2 = "1"
image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["jpeg", "png", "gif", "webp"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["blocking", "json", "rustls-tls"], default-features = false, optional = true }
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
tiny_http = { version = "0.12", optional = true }

pub mod session;

pub use session::*;

# replay-cli

[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/skillsynchq/replay-releases?label=release&color=78716c)](https://github.com/skillsynchq/replay-releases/releases)
[![Website](https://img.shields.io/badge/web-replay.md-78716c)](https://replay.md)

The command-line companion to [Replay](https://replay.md). Browse your local Claude Code and Codex sessions in a TUI, then upload the good ones to share as reviewable threads.

## Install

```bash
curl -sSL https://install.replay.md | sh
replay login
replay              # browse sessions
replay upload <id>  # share one
```

Point it at your local Claude Code or Codex history and it gives you an interactive picker with fuzzy search, a readable conversation view, and a one-command upload to [replay.md](https://replay.md) — where the session becomes a browsable thread with inline diffs, tool calls, and the full back-and-forth.

## Features

- Interactive TUI for browsing local sessions across agents
- Fuzzy search across session titles and content
- Readable conversation view — messages, tool calls, diffs, thinking blocks
- One-command upload to Replay with stable URLs
- Browser-based auth flow (Better Auth)

## Supported agents

| Agent       | Session location                        |
|-------------|-----------------------------------------|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl`         |
| Codex       | `~/.codex/sessions/rollout-*.jsonl`     |

Adding a new agent means implementing the `SessionProvider` trait — see `src/providers/`.

## Commands

```bash
replay              # Launch the TUI (default)
replay browse       # Same as above
replay upload <id>  # Upload a session by ID
replay login        # Authenticate with the Replay server
replay logout       # Remove stored credentials
replay whoami       # Show the current authenticated user
```

### TUI controls

- **↑/↓** or **j/k** — navigate
- **/** — fuzzy search
- **Enter** — open conversation
- **q** / **Esc** — back / quit

## Related projects

- [**replay**](https://github.com/skillsynchq/replay) — the web app at [replay.md](https://replay.md) where uploaded sessions live.

## Development

```bash
cargo check         # type-check
cargo test          # run tests
cargo run           # run (defaults to browse)
cargo build --release
# binary at target/release/replay
```

The TUI in `src/tui/` is structured as an Elm-style MVU loop. New agents are added by implementing `SessionProvider` in `src/providers/`.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. For anything non-trivial, open an issue first so we can talk through the direction.
